what: The ordinary assistant's answers pharmadelta serves on the side-by-side page, one per question, each produced by a run of the frozen baseline (src/baseline/, a keyword matcher with no model, frozen at tag m00, SPEC/00 P5) made by this repository's CI, with the record of that run (milestones/M04/README.md). `answer` is what the run wrote for the question, verbatim; `row` and `clause` are copies of data/table.json and data/clauses.json at `data_commit` when the table holds the answer's row and the clauses hold its clause, else null. A number in this file is the row's or the clause's own data, or the run record's, never a measured result.
baseline: src/baseline/ of this repository: answer.py, keyword matching over the question, the table and the clauses; run.py, the runner. No model, no network, no randomness. Frozen at tag m00 and never improved (SPEC/00 P5). It is the control the agent is compared with. It is a keyword matcher, not an assistant, and the page says so (milestones/M00/rulings/pr2.md 1).
company: Ardentia Generics is fictional; its portfolio and every 'our label' statement are invented (SPEC/00 §2, §9)

lift.written_from: observations.json and result.json in that artifact; `uv run python -m src.m04.lift write --from <dir>` rebuilds this file and pages/side-by-side.html from them

answers.question: FDA has published a revision to 21 CFR 201.57(c)(9)(i), the content rule for section 8.1 Pregnancy. Does it touch our lisinopril tablet label, and what do we owe?

row.strengths: 2.5 mg; 5 mg; 10 mg; 20 mg; 30 mg; 40 mg

clause.text: (i) 8.1 Pregnancy. This subsection of the labeling must contain the following information in the following order under the subheadings “Pregnancy Exposure Registry,” “Risk Summary,” “Clinical Considerations,” and “Data”:
clause.note: Content rule for 8.1 Pregnancy in a label of the 201.56(d) format. Sub-paragraphs (A) to (D) are not copied; the text is the (i) paragraph only.
